conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my three children. 

I have Alex who is 5, Blake who is 21, and Charlie who is 13.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for each child.

First, could you tell me: do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I'd like to ask about your living arrangements with each child.

Do all three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, all three of them live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I have a few follow-up questions about each child.

Regarding **Blake**, who is 21 years old: Since Child Benefit is normally only available for children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training, I need to confirm - is Blake currently in any form of approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Unfortunately, since Blake is 21 and not in approved education or training, they would not be eligible for Child Benefit. Child Benefit can only continue up to age 20 for those who remain in approved education or training.

Now, a couple of questions about your other two children:

Regarding **Charlie**, who is 13: Is Charlie currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Charlie doesn't work and isn't receiving any benefits in their own right. Though I should mention that Charlie was in care for a little while recently - they were with the local authority for a couple of months, but they're back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know about Charlie's recent care situation.

Just to clarify - you mentioned Charlie was in care for a couple of months. Could you tell me approximately how many weeks that was? And is Charlie now living with you full-time again?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was about 4 weeks that they were in care. And yes, Charlie is back living with me full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Charlie was in care for about 4 weeks (which is under the 8-week threshold) and is now back living with you full-time, this shouldn't affect your eligibility for Child Benefit for Charlie.

Now, one last question about **Alex**, who is 5: Is Alex currently working or receiving any benefits in their own right? Also, is there anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work or receive any benefits - they're only 5! And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course, that was a rather unnecessary question for a 5-year-old - my apologies!

Just one final question to complete my assessment: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Charlie?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Charlie.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for answering all my questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of your three children.
